topics.topic: Looking at Earth from 65 Million Light-Years Away
topics.hook: If an alien 65 million light-years away pointed a telescope at Earth right now, they wouldn't see humans—they’d see live dinosaurs.
topics.why_watch: It breaks the intuitive perception of time and space, demonstrating how light travel works in a visually mind-bending way.

topics.topic: The Boötes Void: The Emptiest Place in the Universe
topics.hook: There is a patch of space so empty that if the Milky Way were in the middle of it, we wouldn't have known other galaxies existed until the 1960s.
topics.why_watch: Exploits cosmic existential curiosity and deep-space dread (kenophobia) without leaning into pseudoscience.

topics.topic: The Antikythera Mechanism: The 2,000-Year-Old Analog Computer
topics.hook: In 1901, divers found a bronze lump in a Roman shipwreck. It turned out to be a computer built 1,500 years before modern science caught up.
topics.why_watch: Challenges modern assumptions about ancient technology and presents a genuine, solved historical mystery.

topics.topic: Rogue Waves: The Myth That Turned Out to Be Terrifyingly Real
topics.hook: Until 1995, ocean scientists dismissed 100-foot spontaneous monster waves as drunken sailor folklore—until one actually hit an oil rig.
topics.why_watch: Combines natural disaster fascination with the satisfaction of a myth scientifically proven by modern instruments (Draupner wave).

topics.hook: There is a creature on Earth that can hit 'Ctrl+Z' on aging and turn back into a baby whenever it gets sick or injured.
topics.why_watch: Taps into humanity's eternal obsession with biological immortality and cellular regeneration.

topics.topic: Storing the Entire Internet in a Teaspoon of DNA
topics.hook: Every single YouTube video, movie, and book ever produced could fit inside a container the size of a sugar cube.
topics.why_watch: High-concept biotech trivia that reframes modern data storage challenges with a shocking quantitative comparison.

topics.topic: Phantom Vibration Syndrome: Why Your Phone Vibrates When It Doesn't
topics.hook: Ever reached into your pocket because you felt your phone buzz, only to see zero notifications? Your brain was tricked by a neurological glitch.
topics.why_watch: Universally relatable everyday psychology; viewers immediately recognize the experience in their own lives.

topics.topic: What If You Dropped an Object Down a Hole Through the Earth?
topics.hook: If you drilled a tunnel straight through Earth and jumped in, you wouldn't just fall to the core—you’d become a human pendulum.
topics.why_watch: Classic physics thought experiment with an unexpected answer involving terminal velocity, gravity shifts, and Coriolis force.

topics.topic: The 1908 Tunguska Event: The Explosion Without a Crater
topics.hook: In 1908, a blast flattened 80 million trees across 800 square miles in Siberia, but when researchers arrived, there was no impact crater at all.
topics.why_watch: Compelling factual mystery explaining the mechanics of an airburst meteor with dramatic imagery potential.

topics.hook: Have you ever learned a rare new word or noticed a weird car, and suddenly started seeing it three times a day? You’re not in a simulation.
topics.why_watch: Provides a scientific and cognitive explanation for a spooky sensation most people assume is synchronicity or coincidence.
